languages._comment_version_axis: The language-version axis is the Kotlin COMPILER version (1.0-2.4, 15 real minor lines, each resolving to that line's own latest patch dynamically off Maven Central's org.jetbrains.kotlin:kotlin-stdlib metadata -- the same 'always latest patch of a tracked minor' convention used throughout this project, e.g. Rust's rustc minors, Java's Quarkus/Spring anchor resolution) -- a deliberate, user-confirmed design decision, NOT the JDK version. There is no official Kotlin Docker Hub image (confirmed via a direct registry API 404) and the Kotlin compiler's own runtime JDK floor never moved past 8 even through the K2 rewrite (confirmed live: JDK 8 became mandatory at Kotlin 1.1.2 in 2017 and every source checked as of 2.2 still only requires JDK 8 to RUN kotlinc) -- so unlike Java, JDK version carries no real per-language-version compatibility signal here and is NOT tracked as a compatibility axis at all. Instead JDK (and the Gradle version needed to drive the Kotlin Gradle Plugin, which has its own, much more consequential floor -- see lang_kotlin.py's _BUILD_TOOLCHAIN) is treated purely as an implementation detail chosen per Kotlin line, mirroring how this project already treats OS base-image selection for other languages as generator-internal logic rather than a registry field. All 15 lines are dated live via the GitHub Releases API (JetBrains/kotlin, 299 releases fetched) cross-checked against Maven Central's kotlin-stdlib maven-metadata.xml (every GitHub-tagged stable matches a real published artifact). Kotlin 2.4.10 (2026-07-14) is the latest stable as of this writing; 2.4.20 exists only as a Beta at research time and is correctly NOT tracked (this project's stable-only convention, same as every other language registry).

frameworks.name: Ktor
frameworks.notes: Resolution anchor is ktor-server-core for major 1 (the real, plain-JVM artifact at that time) but ktor-server-core-jvm from major 2 onward -- confirmed live that Ktor's Maven Central layout genuinely split into Kotlin-Multiplatform leaf artifacts exactly at 2.0.0-beta-1 (the '-jvm' suffixed artifact's own maven-metadata.xml starts there; the un-suffixed 'ktor-server-core' becomes a Gradle-Module-Metadata variant-matching root from that point on, still resolvable as a plain dependency coordinate in a real build.gradle.kts -- Gradle's GMM-aware resolver picks the -jvm variant automatically for a JVM project -- but NOT useful for version-list lookups via a raw maven-metadata.xml fetch, hence the anchor switch here). The full version history (1.0.0 through 3.5.2) was fetched as ONE continuous series from ktor-server-core's own maven-metadata.xml, so this framework's own numbering has no gap the way Conscrypt's does. Kotlin compatibility per major uses this project's established lifecycle-window rule (see Java registry's Micronaut/Helidon notes for precedent): a Kotlin line is attributed to whichever Ktor major's active-development window it was actually released during, confirmed against each major's OWN pinned Kotlin version at its first release (read directly from that tag's gradle.properties/libs.versions.toml on GitHub) rather than assumed. Ktor 1.0.0 pins kotlin_version=1.3.10 (confirmed via raw.githubusercontent.com/ktorio/ktor/1.0.0/gradle.properties) -- floor is Kotlin 1.3, not 1.0/1.1/1.2 despite Ktor predating Kotlin 1.4-1.6 chronologically no further than its own 2022-04-11 supersession by 2.0. Ktor 2.0.0 pins kotlin_version=1.6.20 (gradle.properties@2.0.0) -- floor 1.6, ceiling 2.0 (the last Kotlin line released before Ktor 3.0's 2024-10-09 launch; Ktor 2.x's own final patch 2.3.13 shipped 2024-11-20, after 3.0 already existed, but its own dependency floor never moved past what 2.0.0 first required). Ktor 3.0.0 pins kotlin=2.0.20 (libs.versions.toml@3.0.0, a Kotlin 2.0.x patch, not 2.0.0 itself) -- floor attributed to the whole 2.0 line since this registry tracks Kotlin at minor-line granularity; ceiling is 2.4, the newest tracked Kotlin line, since Ktor 3.x is still actively maintained (latest 3.5.2, pinning kotlin=2.3.21) with no successor yet to bound it. Dependency artifacts used: ktor-server-netty (engine) + ktor-server-core, both plain-JVM-resolvable coordinates at every major via the GMM behavior described above.

frameworks.name: Spring Boot
frameworks.notes: Spring Boot 1.x is NOT tracked for Kotlin -- a genuine technical impossibility, not a convenience exclusion (see feedback_no_convenience_exclusions in this project's own memory discipline): Kotlin support in the Spring stack was only added in Spring FRAMEWORK 5.0 (Jan 2017 -- spring.io/blog/2017/01/04/introducing-kotlin-support-in-spring-framework-5-0, confirmed extension functions/null-safety-aware APIs/reified generics for WebFlux all landed there for the first time), and Boot 1.x (2014) predates Framework 5.0 by 3 years; there is no Kotlin DSL, no Jackson-Kotlin-module wiring, nothing to build against. Same reused Maven anchor (spring-boot-starter-parent) and majors as the Java registry -- this is the identical artifact, Kotlin just adds kotlin-reflect + jackson-module-kotlin on the classpath and (optionally) the kotlin('plugin.spring') Gradle plugin for the all-open behavior Spring's proxy-based DI needs on Kotlin's final-by-default classes; no Kotlin-specific starter artifact exists. Boot 2's own per-version Kotlin floor is not directly documented the way 3.0/4.0 are (see below) so this project's lifecycle-window rule is applied here too: Boot 2 was active 2018-03-01 to 3.0's 2022-11-24, and only Kotlin 1.3 onward was released strictly after Boot 2's own launch (1.2, released 2017-11-28, predates Boot 2 and is deliberately excluded rather than assumed retroactively compatible) -- ceiling is 1.7 (released 2022-06-09, the last Kotlin line before Boot 3 existed). Boot 3 and Boot 4's floors ARE directly documented, not window-inferred: Boot 3.0.0 itself pins kotlinVersion=1.7.21 in its own gradle.properties (confirmed live at raw.githubusercontent.com/spring-projects/spring-boot/v3.0.0/gradle.properties) -- floor 1.7 (note this is EARLIER than Boot 2's own window would have ended, i.e. Boot 3 explicitly supports a Kotlin line that already existed under Boot 2 too, which is expected and not a conflict -- a framework's own documented floor can predate its release, unlike the runtime-driven JDK floors in the Java registry that this lifecycle rule was originally built around). Boot 3's ceiling is set at 2.1, immediately below Boot 4's own documented baseline. Boot 4.0 explicitly 'raises the Kotlin baseline to 2.2' per Spring's own release blog (spring.io/blog/2025/12/18/next-level-kotlin-support-in-spring-boot-4, 'switch from Kotlin 1 to Kotlin 2 with a new Kotlin 2.2 baseline') -- floor 2.2, extended through 2.4 (the newest tracked Kotlin line; Boot 4 has no successor yet to bound it). **jackson-module-kotlin (a direct dependency this framework's own build.gradle.kts adds, not a registry-tracked axis) previously always resolved to Maven Central's absolute latest release, on the assumption that any recent release is compatible with whatever Boot itself pulls in** -- disproven by a real batch-test failure: jackson-module-kotlin declares its own kotlin-stdlib version via a <version.kotlin> POM property that rises over time exactly like Ktor's own per-patch pin (2.10.0->1.3.41, 2.13.0->1.5.30, 2.15.0->1.5.32, latest 2.22.1->2.1.21) -- resolving to latest against Kotlin 1.3 or 1.7 put a 2.1.21 stdlib on the classpath that compileKotlin refused to read ('Class kotlin.KotlinVersion was compiled with an incompatible version of Kotlin. The binary version of its metadata is 2.1.0, expected version is 1.1.16'). Fixed with the same live per-patch-walk architecture as _resolve_ktor() (_resolve_jackson_kotlin(), newest-first, first version whose own pin doesn't exceed the target Kotlin line) rather than a static table, for the same reason a static table was already proven insufficient for Ktor. **That fix alone was still insufficient for Boot 3, confirmed via a real Gradle dependencyInsight report**: spring-boot-starter-web transitively pulls spring-boot-starter-json, which imports com.fasterxml.jackson:jackson-bom as a platform() at whatever Jackson version that Spring Boot patch itself resolved to (jackson-bom:2.21.4 for Boot 3.5.16) -- that BOM also manages jackson-module-kotlin's own version, and since a platform() import's recommendation participates in NORMAL (non-enforced) conflict resolution, Gradle picked the BOM's newer 2.21.4 over this project's own deliberately-older, per-line-resolved request, silently pulling a too-new jackson-module-kotlin (and transitively ITS OWN kotlin-reflect:2.1.21) back onto the classpath despite the lower version explicitly declared -- reproducing the identical 'incompatible version of Kotlin' failure the per-line resolution was supposed to prevent. Fixed with a resolutionStrategy.force() of this project's own resolved jackson-module-kotlin version (the same mechanism Quarkus's own BOM-override conflicts already use, which DOES take precedence over a platform()'s recommendation), applied unconditionally for every Spring Boot combo. Also found in the same investigation: Boot 3 has required JDK >=17 since its very first release (not something that crept in at a later patch) -- Kotlin 1.7 (this registry's own documented Boot-3 floor) sits on this project's JDK-11 toolchain tier, confirmed via a real Gradle Module Metadata variant-matching failure ('declares a component compatible with Java 17 and the consumer needed a component compatible with Java 11') resolving Boot 3 to its own absolute latest patch (3.5.16, no per-patch Kotlin-pin drift the way Ktor/http4k have, so 'resolve to latest' is otherwise safe here) -- fixed with a per-(Spring Boot, major 3, Kotlin 1.7)-only _toolchain() override bumping to JDK 17/Gradle 7.6.4-jdk17 (every OTHER Kotlin line registered as Boot-3-compatible, 1.8 onward, already defaults to JDK 17+).

frameworks.name: http4k
frameworks.notes: The second genuinely Kotlin-native (non-JVM-reused) framework tracked -- a purely-functional, dependency-light HTTP toolkit (HttpHandler = (Request) -> Response), no annotations, no DI container. Narrowed to majors 5 and 6 for this first pass (0-4 are real but old, released before http4k adopted the refreshVersions/versions.properties mechanism this registry's own resolution logic depends on -- see below -- and are of lower research/build value; can be added later the same way Java's Tink/Conscrypt entries were narrowed then left open for expansion). http4k releases essentially continuously (automated release-per-merge, confirmed via Maven Central: majors 5 and 6 alone span 48 and 58 real published minors respectively, e.g. 5.0.0.0 through 5.47.0.0, 6.0.0.0 through 6.57.1.0 as of this writing) -- UNLIKE every other framework in this project, 'resolve major to its own absolute latest patch' is NOT safe here: confirmed via a real, dense sweep of http4k's own versions.properties/libs.versions.toml (version.kotlin=X at each sampled tag) that the required Kotlin compiler version drifts CONTINUOUSLY within a single major, not just at major boundaries the way Ktor's ~10 total minors did -- e.g. within major 6 alone: 6.0-6.4 pin kotlin 2.0.21, 6.5-6.17 pin 2.1.20, 6.18-6.24 pin 2.2.20, 6.25-6.54 pin 2.3.x, 6.55+ pin 2.4.0. Given the sheer density (100+ real minors per major) makes a full per-minor floor table (Ktor's own fix) impractical to hand-build and verify, lang_kotlin.py's _resolve_http4k() instead resolves to one of a small number of hand-verified, EXACT checkpoint versions per major (not a live 'latest patch of X.Y' resolution the way every other framework/library in this project works) -- picking the highest checkpoint whose own confirmed Kotlin floor doesn't exceed the target line. This is a deliberate, documented deviation from this registry's universal resolution convention, not an oversight -- every checkpoint's own kotlin pin was individually confirmed via a live fetch of that exact tag's versions.properties/libs.versions.toml, not interpolated or assumed. Compatibility ranges above extend forward through 2.4 (Kotlin metadata is forward- but not backward-readable, same reasoning as Ktor) from each major's own real floor (major 5's earliest checkpoint needs kotlin 1.8.22 at 5.0.0.0; major 6's earliest checkpoint needs kotlin 2.0.21 at 6.0.1.0). Dependency artifacts: http4k-core + http4k-server-undertow (a lightweight embedded server needing no servlet container, matching this project's preference for minimal-footprint app templates), both released in lockstep with http4k-core's own version number. **http4k v6 (Community Edition) set its minimum JVM bytecode target to 21 for the WHOLE major from its very first release** ("From v6, http4k CE will set its minimum supported target JVM version to 21", http4k.org/news/http4k-v6-and-ee/) -- confirmed independently via a real runtime crash resolving major 6's own Kotlin-2.0 checkpoint (6.0.1.0) against Kotlin 2.0's default toolchain tier (JDK 17 in this registry): 'UnsupportedClassVersionError: org/http4k/routing/RoutingHttpHandler has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 65.0), this version only recognizes up to 61.0' (65=JDK21, 61=JDK17), and directly inspecting that checkpoint's own compiled .class bytes (cafe babe 0000 0041, major version 0x41=65) independent of which Kotlin compiler built it. Every other Kotlin line registered as http4k-6-compatible (2.1 onward) already defaults to JDK 21+ in this project's own toolchain tiers, so only Kotlin 2.0 needed a per-(http4k, major 6, Kotlin 2.0) _toolchain() override -- same shape as Spring Boot 3's own JDK17-floor override, and the third framework this exact 'framework's own JDK floor exceeds the target language line's default toolchain tier' conflict has now been found in (after Quarkus's Gradle floor and Micronaut 5's JDK25 floor).

frameworks.name: Micronaut
frameworks.notes: Same coordinate/majors/JDK facts as the Java registry's own Micronaut entry -- reused wholesale. Kotlin annotation-processing MECHANISM genuinely differs by major, confirmed via two real, compounding build/runtime bugs rather than assumed uniform: io.micronaut:micronaut-inject-kotlin as its own separately-published artifact only EXISTS from Micronaut 4.0.0 onward (its own maven-metadata.xml's oldest entry is 4.0.0-M1) -- majors 1-3 have no such artifact at all -- AND that 4.x/5.x jar registers ONLY a KSP SymbolProcessorProvider service (confirmed via direct jar inspection of its META-INF/services/), no javax.annotation.processing.Processor at all, so kapt cannot invoke it (a real docker run confirmed this precisely: the build succeeded with zero errors, kaptKotlin ran, but both endpoints 404'd -- no routes were ever registered, because kapt only understands the Processor SPI and this jar doesn't implement it). Majors 1-3 therefore use kapt against io.micronaut:micronaut-inject-java instead (confirmed via jar inspection at both a major-1-era version, 1.3.7, and a major-3-era version, 3.10.4: this artifact DOES register javax.annotation.processing.Processor) -- the original, pre-KSP mechanism, where kapt generates Java stubs from Kotlin source and micronaut-inject-java processes those stubs exactly as if they were real Java sources. Majors 4/5 use the real `id("com.google.devtools.ksp")` Gradle plugin instead, resolved to the exact KSP release matching the target Kotlin patch (versioned '{kotlin patch}-{ksp release}', e.g. '2.0.21-1.0.28' -- confirmed via com.google.devtools.ksp:symbol-processing-gradle-plugin's own maven-metadata.xml, which needs a raw, unfiltered fetch since this hyphenated scheme doesn't match the stable-release regex this project's shared Maven-version fetcher normally applies) with a same-minor-line fallback if the exact patch has no KSP release yet. Micronaut's own artifacts are plain-JVM bytecode (not Kotlin-Multiplatform metadata) so there is no per-patch Kotlin-COMPILER-version coupling the way Ktor/http4k have -- 'resolve major to latest patch' is exactly as safe here as it already is for Java; the Kotlin-compatibility ranges above are floor-based lifecycle-window inference only (same reasoning already used for this registry's own JDK-side Micronaut/Helidon entries in the Java registry), each major's floor being the Kotlin line current around that major's own release date, extended through 2.4 with no real ceiling. Deliberately does NOT use the official io.micronaut.application Gradle plugin (avoids a second, separately-versioned build-tool-plugin axis, same reasoning as this registry's own Spring Boot entry) -- instead imports the exact same per-major BOM/parent coordinate lang_java.py already established (io.micronaut:micronaut-bom for major 1, io.micronaut:micronaut-parent for majors 2/3, io.micronaut.platform:micronaut-parent for majors 4/5) via Gradle's platform() dependency notation, which reads a POM's <dependencyManagement> exactly the same way a Maven <parent>/import does -- NOTE this BOM/parent coordinate's own version numbers do NOT match micronaut-core's (confirmed via a real Gradle failure resolving a micronaut-core-derived version against io.micronaut.platform:micronaut-parent, which was never published at that exact patch), so framework-version RESOLUTION itself must target the BOM/parent coordinate directly, never micronaut-core. micronaut-serde-jackson is added for majors 3+ only (majors 1/2 rely on Jackson support bundled directly in micronaut-http/-core), same _MICRONAUT_NO_SERDE_MAJORS split as Java's own registry. Major 1's own floor is narrowed to 1.6 (not the lifecycle-window-inferred 1.2) after a real, confirmed failure: Kotlin 1.3 (this project's own JDK-8/Gradle-5.6.4 tier for that line) failed kapt itself with an opaque 'InvocationTargetException (no error message)' during the kaptKotlin task -- a genuine old-JDK-8-era kapt bug, not a config mistake, confirmed by the SAME exact template succeeding cleanly one tier up at Kotlin 1.6 (JDK 11/Gradle 6.9.4), where kaptKotlin real-generated 3 bean classes and the app answered both endpoints correctly. 1.2-1.5 were not individually re-tested one by one -- narrowed together as the same pre-1.6/JDK-8 era, the same 'narrow to the confirmed-working boundary, don't assume the whole range' judgment call already used elsewhere in this registry (e.g. Quarkus's own Kotlin narrowing above). Major 5's own Kotlin 2.2 pairing is EXCLUDED (not just narrowed to a safe subset) after confirming a genuine, unresolvable conflict: Micronaut 5 forces a JDK-25 toolchain (its own documented 'Java 25 baseline', already the JDK floor for this same major in the Java registry) -- confirmed via a real build failure ('...micronaut-http-server-netty:5.1.10 is only compatible with JVM runtime version 25 or newer') that this is a hard Gradle-metadata requirement on the CONSUMING project's own compile target, not just a runtime nicety -- but Kotlin 2.2's own compiler predates JDK 25's GA by ~3 months and cannot target higher than JVM 24 (confirmed via a second real build failure once an explicit jvmTarget=24 override was tried specifically to work around the Kotlin-side ceiling: it only moved the conflict, since Micronaut's own Gradle module metadata then rejects a target-24 consumer just as hard as it rejected the original mismatch). No consuming build can simultaneously satisfy 'Kotlin can't target above 24' and 'Micronaut demands at least 25' -- a genuine technical impossibility for this exact pairing, not a convenience exclusion. Kotlin 2.3+ (released after JDK 25 already existed) has no such ceiling and pairs with Micronaut 5 cleanly via jvmToolchain(25) alone, confirmed via a real build+run+curl. Also found in the same investigation: KSP itself changed its own versioning scheme exactly at Kotlin 2.3.0, from the hyphenated '{kotlin patch}-{ksp release}' format (e.g. '2.0.21-1.0.28') to a plain, hyphen-less scheme where KSP's own version number directly matches Kotlin's (confirmed live via Maven Central) -- lang_kotlin.py's _ksp_version()/_fetch_ksp_raw_versions() now handle both schemes; the raw-fetch regex missing the new format was a real bug that silently produced a broken 'version "None"' literal in the generated build.gradle.kts for any Micronaut-4/5 + Kotlin-2.3+ combo before this fix, now guarded explicitly in write_context() too so a genuinely-unavailable KSP release (e.g. none exists yet for Kotlin 2.4.x) skips the combo cleanly instead of writing a broken file.

frameworks.name: Quarkus
frameworks.notes: Same coordinate/majors/JDK facts as the Java registry's own Quarkus entry -- reused wholesale. Kotlin support (the quarkus-kotlin extension) has existed since Quarkus's very first release (confirmed live: io.quarkus:quarkus-kotlin's own maven-metadata.xml goes all the way back to 1.0.0.Final) -- unlike Spring Boot, there is no 'Kotlin support didn't exist yet' floor to enforce. UNLIKE Micronaut (where this project deliberately avoids the official Gradle plugin), Quarkus genuinely REQUIRES its own build-time augmentation step to function at all -- confirmed by the fact that lang_java.py's own Maven pom.xml already binds quarkus-maven-plugin's 'build' goal into the lifecycle, not just resteasy/jackson dependencies -- so the Kotlin generator uses the real, official `id("io.quarkus")` Gradle plugin (confirmed available on the Gradle Plugin Portal back to 1.0.0.Final, released in exact lockstep with quarkus-bom's own version). Kotlin-compatibility NARROWED to 2.3/2.4 only for every major, after a real, structural conflict was found and confirmed via TWO separate live docker builds (not assumed): Quarkus's own Gradle plugin (latest 3.x patch, 3.38.1) requires Gradle >=8.14 (a real build failure: 'This version of Quarkus is tested with Gradle 8.14 or later', followed by a genuine NoClassDefFoundError on org.gradle.api.artifacts.ResolvableConfiguration under an older Gradle) -- but Kotlin 2.0.21's own Kotlin Gradle Plugin has an INDEPENDENT compatibility CEILING with newer Gradle: the identical compile failure ('void org.jetbrains.kotlin.incremental.IncrementalCompilationFeatures.<init>...', a binary API mismatch) reproduced under BOTH Gradle 8.14.2 and Gradle 9.6.0, ruling out 'just pick a newer Gradle' as a fix. Only Kotlin 2.3/2.4 (whose own default toolchain tier already sits at Gradle 9.6.0, confirmed working end-to-end via a real build+run+curl) are safe; Kotlin lines 1.0-2.2 are excluded here as a genuine technical impossibility for this framework specifically (not a convenience exclusion -- every one of them still works fine with Ktor/Spring Boot/http4k/Micronaut), pending a possible future per-Kotlin-line KGP/Gradle compatibility matrix if this ever needs finer density. REST layer follows the identical per-major package/dependency split already documented in the Java registry's own Quarkus notes: javax.ws.rs/quarkus-resteasy(-jackson) for majors 1/2, jakarta.ws.rs/quarkus-rest-jackson for 3.x onward -- narrowed to 2.3/2.4 uniformly across all three majors as a conservative first pass; only major 3's own Gradle-plugin floor was directly tested, majors 1/2 (whose own latest patches are much older, ~2020-2021-era) may plausibly tolerate a wider range but were not independently re-verified. Packaged as quarkus.package.type=uber-jar (set via application.properties, the only mechanism Quarkus's Gradle-side build-time augmentation reads -- there is no Gradle-DSL equivalent of a Maven <properties> entry) producing app-0.0.0-runner.jar (an explicit `version = "0.0.0"` in build.gradle.kts, matching lang_java.py's own <version>0.0.0</version> convention, keeps this filename predictable -- Gradle's own unset-version default bakes the literal string 'unspecified' into the same filename otherwise, confirmed via a real build). **The 'majors 1/2 may plausibly tolerate a wider range' hedge above was WRONG, confirmed by a real batch-test failure**: at Kotlin 2.3/2.4 (Gradle 9.6.0, this framework's own required floor), major 1's latest patch (1.13.7.Final) failed with 'org/gradle/api/plugins/JavaPluginConvention > org.gradle.api.plugins.JavaPluginConvention' (a class removed outright at Gradle 9.0) and major 2's latest patch (2.16.12.Final, 2023-10-16) failed with "Cannot add a configuration with name 'integrationTestImplementation' as a configuration with that name already exists" (a real, documented quarkusio/quarkus Gradle-plugin bug tied to newer Gradle's auto-registered test-suite configurations, confirmed via web research to affect Gradle 8.x+ and never backported to the already-EOL 2.x line) -- both majors' own Gradle plugins simply predate Gradle 9 (and, for major 1, even parts of Gradle 8) and were never updated for it, since neither major has received a real feature release since Quarkus 3.0 shipped. Root cause confirmed empirically (isolated single-combo rebuilds, not assumed) to be the SHARED Gradle 9.6.0 tier alone -- Gradle 7.6.4 (old enough to predate both removed/changed APIs, still new enough to run this registry's own Kotlin 2.3/2.4 KGP cleanly) builds, runs, and curls correctly for both majors with no other code change. Fixed with a per-(Quarkus,major-1/2) `_toolchain()` override in lang_kotlin.py (gradle:7.6.4-jdk11 / eclipse-temurin:11-jre, jdk downgraded to 11 alongside the Gradle version so the daemon's own bundled JDK matches jvmToolchain() exactly rather than relying on Gradle's toolchain auto-download reaching the network mid-build) -- the same per-major override shape already used for Micronaut 5's JDK25 requirement. A second, independent bug surfaced in the same investigation: quarkus.package.jar.type (this note's own previous wording) is a Quarkus 3.10+-only property name -- silently IGNORED with no error or warning on majors 1/2 (Quarkus just falls back to its fast-jar default, producing quarkus-app/quarkus-run.jar instead of the uber-jar this Dockerfile's COPY expects), confirmed via a real build inspecting the actual output directory. quarkus.package.type (the pre-3.10 name) is confirmed to still work on 3.10+ too, real build+run verified (only a 'has been deprecated' log line, output unaffected) -- so this project now emits quarkus.package.type unconditionally for every major instead of splitting by era.

cryptography_libs.name: JCA
cryptography_libs.notes: Java Cryptography Architecture -- identical to the Java registry's own JCA entry, since Kotlin compiles to the same JVM bytecode and calls java.security/javax.crypto directly with zero wrapper needed. Provider name/version read via java.security.Security.getProviders(), same as Java.

cryptography_libs.name: BouncyCastle
cryptography_libs.notes: Same coordinate, same 16-bucket version history, and same per-bucket PQC-support facts as the Java registry's own BouncyCastle entry (org.bouncycastle:bcprov-jdk18on is plain-Java bytecode, consumed identically from Kotlin -- see _bc_coord() precedent in lang_java.py for the '1.70'-only legacy bcprov-jdk15on switch, reused unchanged). No compatibility restriction against Kotlin lines: BC has no known Kotlin-version sensitivity (it's a provider registered via Security.addProvider(), never touches Kotlin-specific bytecode features).

cryptography_libs.name: Tink
cryptography_libs.notes: Same coordinate and per-bucket PQC facts (1.21 = first ML-DSA-87 signature support, 1.22 adds SLH-DSA + ML-DSA-44, still no KEM-side PQC as of 1.22) as the Java registry's own Tink entry -- pure-Java, consumed unchanged from Kotlin, same AeadConfig.register()/registerStandardKeyTypes() version-split logic (see _tink_touch_line() precedent in lang_java.py). Buckets 1.0-1.6 (Tink's own pre-1.7 history, tracked in the Java registry) are deliberately NOT carried over here -- narrowed to 1.7 onward to keep this framework's very first Kotlin-registry pass to the still-actively-relevant window rather than mechanically duplicating Java's full 23-bucket history; can be extended backward on request the same way Java's own BC/Tink entries were expanded from milestone-only to full-density. Buckets 1.19-1.22 are narrowed to Kotlin 1.5+ after a real runtime crash: 'java.lang.UnsupportedClassVersionError: com/google/crypto/tink/aead/AeadConfig has been compiled by a more recent version of the Java Runtime (class file version 55.0), this version of the Java Runtime only recognizes class file versions up to 52.0' at Kotlin 1.3/1.4 (this project's own JDK-8 tier) -- this is the SAME already-documented fact as the Java registry's own Tink entry ('Tink dropped Java 8 support at 1.19.0'), just missed when this Kotlin entry was first written; it needed a real batch-test crash to resurface rather than being carried over from the already-confirmed Java-side finding. Also found in the same batch test: Tink genuinely needs the google() Gradle repository declared (androidx.annotation:annotation, a real non-optional transitive dependency in Tink's own POM, is not published to Maven Central at all -- confirmed via a direct 404 -- only to Google's Maven repo) -- fixed in lang_kotlin.py's shared repositories{} block, not scoped to Tink specifically since it's harmless when unused. **A second, unrelated Quarkus-only bug found via a real batch test**: Tink 1.16+ embeds a protobuf runtime-version check in its own generated code (com.google.protobuf.RuntimeVersion, part of protobuf-java's gencode-version-checking feature added in its 3.25.x/4.x era) -- under Quarkus majors 1/2 specifically, a real 'NoClassDefFoundError: com/google/protobuf/RuntimeVersion$RuntimeDomain' crashed every request at runtime (build succeeded, only visible via a real docker run), because quarkus-bom pins protobuf-java to an old, pre-RuntimeVersion release (3.14.0 for major 1, 3.22.0 for major 2, confirmed live via each BOM's own POM) and, being imported as enforcedPlatform, that pin silently overrides Tink's own newer requirement the same way it already overrode kotlin-stdlib's version. Major 3's own BOM already pins a new-enough protobuf-java, which is why only majors 1/2 hit this. Fixed with a second resolutionStrategy.force() entry alongside the existing kotlin-stdlib one, forcing protobuf-java to whatever version Tink's own POM actually declares (fetched live via lang_kotlin.py's _tink_protobuf_version(), not hardcoded, since this floor moves with every Tink release) -- applied unconditionally whenever the library is Tink, matching how the kotlin-stdlib force is already applied regardless of whether a given major actually needs it.

cryptography_libs.name: Conscrypt
cryptography_libs.notes: Same coordinate as the Java registry's own Conscrypt entry -- JNI-native provider, consumed identically from Kotlin via Security.addProvider(Conscrypt.newProvider()). Same PLATFORM LIMITATION applies unchanged regardless of calling language: neither bucket bundles ARM64/aarch64 native libraries (only the still-prerelease 2.6-alpha series does) -- will fail with UnsatisfiedLinkError on an arm64 host; see the Java registry's own Conscrypt notes for the full detail. Narrowed to the two most recent stable minors (2.4, 2.5) for this first Kotlin-registry pass rather than mechanically duplicating Java's full 10-bucket history -- can be extended backward on request.

cryptography_libs.name: KotlinCrypto
cryptography_libs.notes: The one genuinely Kotlin-native (not JVM-reused-from-Java) crypto library tracked in this registry -- github.com/KotlinCrypto, group org.kotlincrypto(.hash/.macs/.core/.bitops), a Kotlin-Multiplatform hash/MAC/secure-random suite. Anchor artifact is hash:sha2-jvm (org.kotlincrypto.hash:sha2-jvm, the JVM leaf of its KMP split -- same '-jvm' suffix convention as Ktor 2.x+/KotlinCrypto's own whole ecosystem) since SHA-2 is its most broadly-used module; touch code exercises Sha256(). Bucketed at the '0.MINOR' line (0.2 through 0.8, 7 buckets, each resolving to that line's own latest patch dynamically -- e.g. 0.2 has 8 real patches 0.2.0-0.2.7) rather than every individual patch, matching this project's own established minor-line granularity (the same unit Java's BouncyCastle/Tink entries use). All 7 buckets' first-patch dates confirmed live via repo1.maven.org's Last-Modified header (org/kotlincrypto/hash/sha2-jvm/{version}/sha2-jvm-{version}.pom for 0.2.0/0.3.0/0.4.0/0.5.1/0.6.0/0.7.0/0.8.0 -- note 0.5's own first published patch is 0.5.1, no 0.5.0 was ever released, confirmed via the artifact's own maven-metadata.xml version list). Kotlin-compatibility floors above are EMPIRICAL, not read from KotlinCrypto's own build config -- confirmed the hard way after a real batch test found 62 build failures: KotlinCrypto's own gradle/libs.versions.toml 'kotlin' key (the version its OWN release is BUILT with, e.g. bucket 0.2 shows kotlin=1.8.21) turned out to be a red herring for consumer compatibility, since KotlinCrypto (like many real Kotlin-Multiplatform libraries) deliberately targets an OLDER consumer-side language/API version than its own build tooling uses -- confirmed directly: bucket 0.2, built with kotlin 1.8.21 tooling, actually works fine for a consumer targeting Kotlin 1.7. The real floors were instead read directly off the actual pass/fail matrix of a genuine batch test run across all 15 tracked Kotlin lines: 0.2/0.3 first succeed at Kotlin 1.7 (fail at 1.6), 0.4/0.5/0.6 first succeed at 1.8 (fail at 1.7), 0.7/0.8 first succeed at 2.1 (fail at 2.0) -- a clean, consistent three-tier boundary with no anomalies across the whole matrix. IMPORTANT negative finding, confirmed via the suite's own module list: KotlinCrypto is classical-crypto only (hash functions, HMAC/KMAC, a SecureRandom abstraction, low-level bit/endian utilities) -- it has NO KEM or signature algorithms and NO post-quantum support at all, and is not a symmetric-cipher/TLS library either. This is the intentional contrast this entry exists to surface: a real, actively-maintained, idiomatic-Kotlin crypto library that is nonetheless NOT a PQC option -- liboqs-kotlin (below) is this registry's only PQC-capable entry that isn't reused wholesale from Java.

cryptography_libs.name: liboqs-kotlin
cryptography_libs.notes: liboqs-java (github.com/open-quantum-safe/liboqs-java), the official OQS-org JNI wrapper, consumed unchanged from Kotlin (plain public API: org.openquantumsafe.KeyEncapsulation/.Signature, zero porting needed -- same 'any plain-Java-API library needs no Kotlin-specific wrapper' fact as JCA/BouncyCastle/Tink/Conscrypt above, just without a Maven Central artifact backing it). CONFIRMED liboqs-java is NOT published to Maven Central (org/openquantumsafe/liboqs-java/maven-metadata.xml returns HTTP 404) -- unlike Ruby's roqs or PHP's php-liboqs which resolve through their own language's normal package registry, this binding must be BUILT FROM SOURCE in the same Dockerfile: git-clone liboqs itself (the C library) at a pinned tag, cmake+ninja build+install it, then git-clone liboqs-java and 'mvn package' it against the just-installed liboqs, producing a local jar consumed as a Gradle file-tree/flatDir dependency rather than a normal mavenCentral() coordinate -- the identical multi-stage shape as lang_php.py's php-liboqs handling (git-clone liboqs -> cmake --target install -> git-clone the language wrapper -> build against it -> multi-stage COPY of just the compiled .so/.jar into a slim runtime, discarding the ~250MB+ build toolchain), reused as the precedent rather than invented fresh. 'module' is the literal string 'source-build' (this registry's marker for 'no real package-registry identifier to check', parallel to Node's own 'built-in' marker convention) -- lang_kotlin.py's own git-tag table drives resolution instead of a live package-registry lookup, so check_updates.py's generic maven-enumerator correctly skips this entry (module isn't a 'group:artifact' string) the same way it already skips every other language's true built-ins. Only liboqs-java's latest release, 0.3.0 (2025-04-25, adds derandomized-seed KEM keygen), is tracked for this first pass -- 0.1.0 (2020-07-08) and 0.2.0 (2025-01-24) exist but are not carried over, the same 'narrow to the actively-relevant window first, extend on request' judgment call already applied to this registry's own Tink/Conscrypt entries above. liboqs-java's own pom.xml requires JDK >= 8 to build (its CI runs Ubuntu 24.04 + OpenJDK 21) and uses a conventional Maven build (git-clone + mvn package), not Gradle, for the wrapper jar itself -- only the CONSUMING Kotlin app uses Gradle.
